analysis:
The PR only changes docs/reference/configuration.md, adding two table rows at head lines 415-416: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED. Both default on, accept an exact `0` to disable, and are documented as forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The patch contains no executable code, so no code-level regression is observable here. Referenced readers are ToolStreamPreparation.swift (streamsToolCallsByDefault) and ReasoningPromptProbe.swift (seedsPlainTailContentByDefault); neither was supplied, and I could not verify the documented behavior or whether the LaunchAgent passthrough allowlist actually contains these names.

Security-relevant integration questions for the code-side review:
(1) Streaming tool-call fragments before each call is validated at frame close. Fragments of a call that later fails validation would already have reached the consumer. This is a consumer-facing correctness and integrity concern, not a provider-confidentiality one, and it relates loosely to T-007/T-008.
(2) The streamed chunks must still be encrypted through the existing per-request response encryption path (T-008, fail closed on encryption failure). Streaming earlier must not add a plaintext or unencrypted path.
(3) Seeding content state for Qwen streams (the THINK_CONTENT_SEED row) could cause reasoning text to be emitted as content if the prompt tail is misdetected. That would be a possible disclosure of reasoning to the consumer, an output-format concern rather than a trust-boundary change.
(4) Neither toggle touches the prefix cache (T-041), attestation, authorization, keys or any other threat-model asset, and neither adds new env-var attack surface beyond the provider's own environment, which the operator already controls (TB-003).

No finding is raised, since the documentation change alone does not establish a security regression. A reviewer of the Swift sources should verify the points above.
